extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system (computational algebraists/mathematicians) working with abelian and permutation groups
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/tutorial material describing how to construct, manipulate and query abelian groups and permutation groups in Magma, including constructors, access functions, invariants, and common operations. Includes examples and notes on differences between categories (e.g., GrpAb vs GrpFP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element construction and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of an abelian group can be constructed by coercion expressions (e.g., g := 4*w - 5*x + z;) and are printed in a canonical additive form (e.g., 4*w - 5*x + z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: g := 4*w - 5*x + z; print g; prints 4*w - 5*x + z. The printed form for abelian group elements is always the same (canonical form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative generator coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has only one generator e1, then A!a1 may be used as an alternative to A![a1] to coerce an integer into the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print FreeAbelianGroup(1)!8; prints 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementToSequence / Eltseq behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementToSequence(a) or Eltseq(a) returns the sequence [a1, ..., an] corresponding to element a = a1 e1 + ... + ar er.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print ElementToSequence(g); outputs [ 4, -5, 0, 1 ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition and scalar multiplication on abelian group elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition is the main arithmetic operation; operators + and - are available; scalar m*a sums m copies of element a (negative m returns |m| copies of -a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print 5*g, -5*g; showing 5*g and -5*g results. Use +/− for element arithmetic and m*a for repeated sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: sub constructor for subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: The sub< Parent | generators > constructor creates a subgroup of an abelian group (or any group category) generated by given elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: F4s := sub< F4 | g, y+z >; prints subgroup description and type information.

rubrics_metrics.name: quo constructor for finitely-presented abelian groups (quotients)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quo< G | relations > constructor creates quotients (finitely-presented abelian groups) presented by generators and relations; relations may be given as equations r1 = r2 = ... = rk or as individual relators ri interpreted as ri = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: F4q := quo<F4 | 28*w - 35*x + 7*z = 0, w - 7*z = 2*y>; returns group and can also return the natural homomorphism as second return value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality testing / canonical form distinction (GrpAb vs GrpFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abelian group elements (GrpAb) have canonical forms and can be tested for equality; finitely-presented groups (GrpFP) do not generally have canonical forms and elements may not be testable for equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of canonical forms, printed representations of abelian group elements are always the same. In GrpFP, generator printed forms may be expressions rather than simple names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators printing behaviour in quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: Generators assigned names by the constructor (e.g., s,t,u,v) are not necessarily printed by those names; printed forms are expressions in those identifiers reflecting their images in the quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print t; may print an expression like 5*s + t - 10*u - 35*v; equality testing against that expression returns true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations() returns relations with $.i printed generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations(G) returns a sequence of relations of the group, but generators in this sequence are printed as $.i since they are regarded as elements of the corresponding free abelian group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: R := Relations(F4q); print R; prints relations like [ $.1 - 2*$.3 - 7*$.4 = 0, ... ]. Parent(LHS(R[1])) shows the free abelian group context.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianGroup constructor (from generators and relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianGroup< e1, ..., ei | relations in the ei > constructs a finitely-presented abelian group directly without explicitly creating a free abelian group first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: F4qB<s,t,u,v> := AbelianGroup< s, t, u, v | 28*s - 35*t + 7*v, s - 7*v = 2*u >; prints group isomorphic structure and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianGroup only forms quotient of free abelian group; quo needed for non-free parents
rubrics_metrics.description: The AbelianGroup constructor only forms the quotient of a free abelian group; to construct the quotient of an abelian group that is not free use the quo constructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given where F4qBq := quo< F4qB | 8*s + t = 2*v = u - 9*t >; produces expected quotient and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification / structure theorem application and invariants functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every finitely-generated abelian group A is isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclic groups described by torsion invariants [n1,...,nr] and torsion-free rank t; Magma provides functions to obtain these invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions: TorsionInvariants(A) returns [n1,...,nr]; TorsionFreeRank(A) returns t; Invariants(A) returns torsion invariants followed by t zeros. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: TorsionSubgroup and TorsionFreeSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: TorsionSubgroup(A) returns the largest torsion subgroup (direct sum of finite cyclic factors); TorsionFreeSubgroup(A) returns the torsion-free subgroup (free group on t generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print TorsionSubgroup(A); print TorsionFreeSubgroup(A); output shows decomposition and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and p-primary invariants and components
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimaryInvariants(A) returns the sequence of prime-power invariants; pPrimaryInvariants(A,p) returns invariants that are powers of p; pPrimaryComponent(A,p) returns the subgroup corresponding to the p-primary invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print PrimaryInvariants(A); print pPrimaryInvariants(A,2); print pPrimaryComponent(A,5); with example outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct abelian group from invariants (AbelianGroup([Q]))
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianGroup(Q) constructs an abelian group in GrpAb with invariant sequence Q (zero denotes C_infty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AbelianGroup([2,6,6,6,30,60,0,0,0]) returns a group isomorphic to the previously defined A.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianGroup(C, Q) constructs abelian group in other category C
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianGroup(C, Q) constructs an abelian group in category C given invariant sequence Q; in categories other than GrpFP none of the invariants may be zero (no infinite cyclic components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AbelianGroup(GrpPerm, [2,6,6,6,30,60]) returns a permutation group acting on a set with specified order.

rubrics_metrics.name: DirectProduct called DirectSum in abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic DirectProduct function is named DirectSum in the abelian group category for obvious reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DS := DirectSum(A, F4q); prints resulting abelian group decomposition and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random element generation for abelian groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is finite, Random(A) returns a random element. If infinite, create a RandomProcess(A) and use Random(P) to obtain pseudo-random elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: P := RandomProcess(DS); print Random(P); repeated calls produce pseudo-random elements expressed in generator basis. RandomProcess has two parameters (not explained here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group action definition and natural G-set / degree
rubrics_metrics.description: An action φ: X × G → X must satisfy ((x,g)φ,h)φ = (x,gh)φ and (x,1_G)φ = x; the natural G-set for a permutation group is the finite set X it acts on, and its cardinality n is the degree of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation x^g for image; in Magma every natural G-set must be finite and often is {1,..,n} (standard G-set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating Symmetric groups (Sym(n) and Sym(T))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sym(n) constructs the symmetric group on {1,..,n}. Sym(T) constructs the symmetric group acting on a non-standard enumerated or indexed set T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: s5 := Sym(5); fruits := Sym({"apple","pear","fig"}); print GSet(s5) shows GSet{1..5} and non-standard examples print corresponding GSet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation representation forms and coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutations may be specified as mapping form (sequence of G-set elements) or as product of disjoint cycles; either form must be preceded by the group and a ! to coerce (e.g., s5![3,5,1,4,2] or s5!(1,3)(2,5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cycle form omits 1-cycles; permutations are always printed in cycle form. Representations are always in terms of the elements of the natural G-set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity permutation notation
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity permutation is represented by Id(G) or G!1, where G is the permutation group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Id(G) or coerce 1 into G to get the identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication and exponentiation conventions for permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication operator is * and exponentiation is ^; Magma multiplies permutations left-to-right (i.e., the order shown in examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: b := s5!(1,2,3,4); print a*b, b*a, b^2, b^-1; demonstrates left-to-right multiplication and inverses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Even / odd permutation tests and cycle structure
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEven(g) returns true if g is an even permutation; IsOdd(g) analogous. CycleStructure(g) returns a sequence of pairs <cycle_length, number_of_cycles> describing cycle decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print IsEven(s5!(1,5)(2,4,3)), IsEven(s5!(1,5)(2,4)); and CycleStructure example showing [<5,1>, <2,2>, <1,4>].

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing permutation subgroups: sub and PermutationGroup constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sub<Sym(X) | generators> to create a subgroup of Sym(X) or PermutationGroup<n | generators> (or PermutationGroup<T | generators>) to construct permutation groups without explicit parent reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show creating s6subgp := sub<s6 | ...>; gp := PermutationGroup<6 | ...>; and equality between the two constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard group constructors and projective/affine group functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard functions (Sym, Alt, CyclicGroup, etc.) create commonly used permutation groups. Projective and affine group constructors (e.g., ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup(n,q), AffineGeneralLinearGroup(n,q), etc.) return two values: the group G acting on the standard G-set and an indexed set P of vectors defining the corresponding objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists many constructors with domain restrictions (e.g., n ≥ 2 for projective groups). Example: p33, pts := ProjectiveGammaUnitaryGroup(3,3); Degree(p33) and pts illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product constructions (DirectProduct, TensorProduct, WreathProduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions DirectProduct(H,K), DirectProduct(Q), TensorProduct(H,K)/TensorProduct(Q), WreathProduct(H,K)/WreathProduct(Q) form direct, tensor/wreath products of permutation groups with appropriate actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: DirectProduct(Sym(8), Alt(4)); DirectProduct([Z3 : i in [1..3]]) producing a 3^something order example and printed generators and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image computation notation (x^g, S^g, Q^g) and Image(g,x)
rubrics_metrics.description: x^g or Image(g,x) computes the image of point x under permutation g; S^g or Image(g,S) computes image of a set of points; Q^g or Image(g,Q) for sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print 4^(a*c); prints 5. And [1,2,5]^(a*c) yields [6,7,2]. Table 32.4 summarizes notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation group access functions (GSet, Set, Degree, Support, Fix, Generators, Ngens, Set(G), FormalSet(G), Generic(G))
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of access functions provides information about a permutation group's natural G-set, its underlying enumerated set, degree, support, fixed points, generators, number of generators, the set of all elements (for small groups), the formal set, and the symmetric group in which G is naturally embedded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sequence showing G := PermutationGroup<6 | ...>; X := GSet(G); Set(X); Support(G); Fix(G); print om eq ($1 join $2); demonstrates relations between underlying set, support and fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity and regularity tests and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: IsTransitive(G) returns true if G is transitive. Transitivity(G) returns maximum k such that G is k-transitive. IsTransitive(G,k), IsSharplyTransitive(G,k), IsFrobenius(G), IsRegular(G), IsSemiregular(G,S) provide related tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Transitivity(PGL(2,9)) returns 3; Transitivity(cube) returns 1. Use IsTransitive(G,k) to test specific k-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbits, Orbit notation and Orbits(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbit(G,x) or x^G returns the orbit of point x as a G-set. Orbits(G) returns all orbits as a sequence of G-sets where the ith G-set contains the points of the ith orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bgp := sub<cube | b>; print 1^bgp, 2^bgp; Orbits(bgp) prints all orbits. Orbits are returned as GSets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizers and Transversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Stabilizer(G,x) returns subgroup of elements fixing x; Stabilizer(G,S) and Stabilizer(G,Q) for sets and sequences. Transversal(G,H) returns (i) an indexed set T of right coset representatives for G over H and (ii) a transversal mapping φ: G → T giving canonical coset representative for each g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: stab7 := Stabilizer(cube,7); t,m := Transversal(cube,stab7); t lists coset representatives with first element in stab7; m is mapping from G to T. Use m(g) to find coset representative index.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate for G-set elements, subsets and sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: IsConjugate(G,x,y) tests whether x and y in a G-set are conjugate in G and, if so, returns a conjugating element. Analogous functions test conjugacy for k-subsets and sequences of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cj,g := IsConjugate(stab7,3,6) returns true and a conjugating element g; IsConjugate(cube,{2,4},{3,6}) returns true and a permutation mapping {2,4} to {3,6}.
